title: Plus, Minus or Glue
statement:
You are given a string of digits. Between every two neighbouring digits you choose one of three things: write `+`, write `-`, or write nothing (gluing the digits into one longer number). The first number has no sign in front. This gives an arithmetic expression.

A number may not have leading zeros unless it is exactly the single digit `0`; an expression that contains a number like `05` or `007` is not allowed. Count the allowed expressions whose value equals `T`.

## Input
The first line contains the digit string. The second line contains `T`.

## Output
Print the number of allowed expressions with value `T`.

## Constraints
- `1 <= length <= 11`
- `|T| <= 10^12`
